legend: Abhinav is a scientist who works in the field of perfect arrays. What's a perfect array you ask, let me explain —
A perfect array of size n$$$n$$$ is made by performing n$$$n$$$ perfect operations on an empty array and –

The p$$$p$$$-th perfect operation involves choosing a random integer q$$$q$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and p$$$p$$$ (1≤q≤p)$$$(1\leq q \leq p)$$$, and inserting it in the q$$$q$$$-th position. So, for instance if before the p$$$p$$$-th operation array was like A1,A2...Aq−1,Aq,Aq+1....Ap−1$$$A_{1},A_{2}...A_{q-1},A_{q},A_{q+1}....A_{p-1}$$$, then after the p$$$p$$$-th operation array becomes A1,A2...Aq−1,q,Aq,Aq+1,Aq+2....Ap−1$$$A_{1},A_{2}...A_{q-1},q,A_{q},A_{q+1},A_{q+2}....A_{p-1}$$$.

Harsh wants to become Abhinav's assistant and to check Harsh's intelligence, Abhinav gives him an array Arr$$$Arr$$$ of size n$$$n$$$ and asks him if it is a perfect array or not. And if Arr$$$Arr$$$ is a perfect array, Harsh is required to give the sequence of n$$$n$$$ operations that built up Arr$$$Arr$$$.
Harsh is too dumb to solve this and asks for your help.
input: The first line of input contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤200)$$$(1 \leq n \leq 200)$$$ – the size of given array.
The next line of input contains n$$$n$$$ integers, Arr1,Arr2,....Arrn$$$Arr_{1}, Arr_{2},....Arr_{n}$$$ (1≤Arri≤N)$$$(1 \leq Arr_{i} \leq N)$$$ – the elements of given array.
output: If the given array is not perfect then print "NO".
Else, in the first line print "YES" and in the next line print the sequence of n$$$n$$$ operations that built up the array.
note: 1$$$1$$$-st operation – Add 1$$$1$$$ at 1$$$1$$$-st index. Array becomes [1]$$$[1]$$$
2$$$2$$$-nd operation – Add 1$$$1$$$ at 1$$$1$$$-st index. Array becomes [1,1]$$$[1,1]$$$
3$$$3$$$-rd operation – Add 2$$$2$$$ at 2$$$2$$$-nd index. Array becomes [1,2,1]$$$[1,2,1]$$$
In the second sample testcase, there is no possible sequence of operations that can form the array [2,2]$$$[2,2]$$$.
